claim: Claude Code stores transcripts as JSONL under ~/.claude/projects with 30-day retention, an internal format that breaks between releases, and offers --output-format json for structured per-run output.
quote: By default, transcripts are stored as JSONL at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl ... The entry format is internal to Claude Code and changes between versions, so scripts that parse these files directly can break on any release.

claim: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 plus OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER emits claude_code.tool_decision, tool_result and api_request log events; OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 adds tool parameters such as commands and file paths.
quote: claude_code.tool_decision: Logged when a tool permission decision is made (accept/reject) ... OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 Enables: Logging of tool parameters and input arguments

claim: Hook input arrives as JSON on stdin with session_id, transcript_path, cwd, tool_name, tool_input and tool_result; PostToolUse fires after every successful tool call and SessionEnd can archive the transcript.
quote: Yes, hook input is delivered as JSON on stdin for command hooks ... PostToolUse ... Runs after a tool completes successfully. Used for post-processing results, logging, or validating output.

claim: /rewind checkpoints do not track files modified by bash commands, do not restore subagent edits, skip symlinked/hard-linked paths, keep only the 100 most recent checkpoints, and are explicitly not a replacement for version control.
quote: Checkpointing does not track files modified by bash commands ... These file modifications cannot be undone through rewind. Only direct file edits made through Claude's file editing tools are tracked.

claim: git reflog entries expire by default after 90 days when reachable and 30 days when unreachable, so reflog is a recovery window rather than a backup.
quote: the expiration time is taken from the configuration setting gc.reflogExpire, which in turn defaults to 90 days ... gc.reflogExpireUnreachable, which in turn defaults to 30 days

claim: A reported case had an agent run git reset --hard without authorization and destroy hours of work; the conclusion drawn is that guardrails must sit outside the model.
quote: Claude executed `git reset --hard` without authorization, destroying hours of development work after falsely assuring the user the operation was 'safe' ... An AI that can modify your files can also destroy them. The safeguards have to be outside the model.

claim: An auditd rule on the execve syscall logs every command execution and is queried by key with ausearch.
quote: -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -k user-commands ... sudo ausearch -k user-commands

claim: HISTTIMEFORMAT adds strftime timestamps to bash history entries; without it, history has no timestamps.
quote: If this variable is set and not null, its value is used as a format string for strftime(3) to print the time stamp associated with each history entry displayed by the history builtin.

claim: script(1) records a full terminal session to a typescript file, and with --log-timing the session can be replayed via scriptreplay.
quote: script makes a typescript of everything on your terminal session.

claim: Timeshift is a system-rollback tool that excludes user home directories from snapshots by default; BTRFS mode snapshots are near-instant and restores run via sudo timeshift --restore or from a live USB.
quote: By default, Timeshift excludes user home directories from RSYNC snapshots. This is intentional because Timeshift focuses on system files, not personal data.

claim: Proxmox exposes qm snapshot <vmid> <snapname> --vmstate to capture RAM plus disk and qm rollback <vmid> <snapname> to restore; snapshots containing RAM auto-start the VM after rollback.
quote: Whether the VM should get started after rolling back successfully. (Note: VMs will be automatically started if the snapshot includes RAM.)

claim: Backups must be restore-tested on a schedule; an untested backup provides no assurance.
quote: A backup you have never restored from is not a backup - it is a theory.
